articles.title: The Sony Aibo was a robot revolution dressed like a dog
articles.summary:
In the 1990s, Sony was absolutely convinced that we were on the precipice of a robot takeover. Pretty soon, the company decided, we’d all be living among countless humanoid robots. Some would be our coworkers; others would be our friends; and at least one would be our pet. And “pet” was exactly what Sony was going for when it created the Aibo. It was supposed to be part of the family.
The Sony Aibo was a robot revolution dressed like a dog
On Version History: How a robot dog became a family member, but not exactly a huge hit.
On this episode of Version History, we go back in time and tell the story of the Aibo. David Pierce is joined by The Verge’s Victoria Song and Jennifer Pattison Tuohy, and together they discuss the origins of this remarkable robot dog, and its impressive success and longevity. They also try to figure out why Aibo had such an effect on its owners, what Sony got right (and wrong) about robots, and whether the idea of a robo-pet will ever be a global phenomenon.

articles.title: Pentagon Renames CDAO ‘Super Intelligence Office’
articles.summary:
The Pentagon on Friday renamed its Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO) the Super Intelligence Office, adopting the terminology President Donald Trump has directed federal agencies to use instead of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
Cameron Stanley continues to lead the office as Chief Super Intelligence Officer for the Department of War (DoW), with Andrew Mapes serving as Principal Deputy Super Intelligence Officer. Stanley took over as the Pentagon’s chief digital and AI officer in January after leading national security transformation at Amazon Web Services. He previously led Project Maven, the Pentagon’s military AI initiative.
The Department of War moved the office’s public resources, procurement information and partnership portals to SI.mil domain and said existing programs, solicitations and defense partnerships would continue without interruption. The office’s portfolio includes the Maven Smart System, an AI-enabled intelligence and targeting platform, and the War Data Platform, a central hub for military data.
“This redesignation is a clear signal of where the Department of War is going,” said Stanley. “We have moved beyond experimental prototypes. As the Super Intelligence Office our mission is to harness the full power of sovereign Super Intelligence to ensure decisive military superiority across every domain.”

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: Google : l'IA capte tant de recherches que des annonceurs n'arrivent plus à dépenser leur budget
articles.summary:
Deux semaines après une chute de plus de 12 % en Bourse, qui avait effacé environ 500 milliards de dollars de capitalisation, Alphabet voit le malaise gagner le cœur de son réacteur, la publicité. Un annonceur américain, client depuis sept ans, ne parviendrait plus à écouler son budget quotidien d’environ 2 000 dollars, faute de vues et de clics à acheter. Il met en cause les assistants IA, qui répondent désormais à des questions qui passaient hier par une recherche classique. Six annonceurs et dirigeants d’agence auraient déjà basculé une partie de leurs budgets vers Meta.
Les acheteurs de pub passent leurs dépenses au crible
Dix-huit acheteurs média passent au crible entre 10 et 30 % des budgets de recherche confiés à Google. Certains se disent prêts à déplacer rapidement une partie de ces sommes vers d’autres canaux, Meta en tête, si les performances fléchissent. Le 2 novembre, le groupe a d’ailleurs déplacé les Aperçus IA vers la colonne de droite des résultats sur ordinateur, un emplacement moins central, pour les recherches de marque. Ces requêtes, qui portent le nom d’une entreprise ou d’un produit, comptent parmi les plus disputées de la régie, les annonceurs achetant souvent leur propre nom pour verrouiller le haut de page.
Au troisième trimestre, les revenus de la recherche ont pourtant encore progressé de 12 %, après 17 % au trimestre précédent. Les clics payants gagnent 8 % et le coût par clic 4 %, signe que la régie vend toujours plus d’espaces, un peu plus cher.…

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert…

articles.title: Papelera de WhatsApp: qué es, dónde está y para qué sirve

La papelera de WhatsApp no es una carpeta donde se guarden temporalmente los archivos eliminados. En realidad, la aplicación de Meta cuenta con un administrador de almacenamiento que permite identificar fotografías, videos, audios y documentos que ocupan memoria en el celular.
WhatsApp permite revisar el contenido multimedia que más espacio consume, incluidos los archivos reenviados muchas veces y el material descargado desde los canales.
Desde esa herramienta, cada usuario puede seleccionar qué conservar y qué eliminar sin borrar conversaciones completas.
Antes de eliminar contenido, conviene comprobar que no se trate de documentos, fotografías o videos importantes. Algunos archivos pueden descargarse otra vez desde el chat, pero otros podrían no estar disponibles si fueron borrados de la conversación o de los servidores de Meta.
Dónde está la papelera de WhatsApp
Lo que suele identificarse como la papelera es el administrador de almacenamiento. Esta función permite localizar fotografías, videos y otros documentos que ocupan espacio en el dispositivo.
Para acceder a los archivos reenviados muchas veces, hay que ingresar en Ajustes, seleccionar Almacenamiento y datos y después Administrar almacenamiento.
Para qué sirve la papelera de WhatsApp
El administrador de almacenamiento sirve para localizar contenido que puede haberse acumulado con el tiempo.

articles.title: New Windows zero-day turns Microsoft's own security fix into a path to full system access
articles.summary:
Facepalm: Last year, Microsoft started digitally signing the log files of a Windows component that attackers had been abusing for years. The idea was that any tampered log would simply get rejected. But that same safeguard is now the way in for a new zero-day that lets a standard user take complete control of a PC. Ironically, the attack needs Microsoft's own antivirus running to pull it off.
This latest exploit is called SignDrop. It comes from Abdelhamid Naceri, a former Microsoft employee who has been dumping unpatched Windows bugs online under the name Nightmare Eclipse since April. He published the code on GitHub on Tuesday, just as Microsoft was rolling out its November security updates.
A bug like this is notable because it can turn a minor infection into a full takeover. Malware that slips in through a shady download usually runs with the same limited rights as the user. SignDrop would let it climb to the very top, where it can switch off security tools and dig in for good. And since the code is public, anyone can try it.
The bug sits in the Common Log File System (CLFS), which apps and drivers across Windows use to keep their logs. The problem is a small companion file it creates next to each log to help with recovery. That file inherits its permissions from the log, so whoever set up the log gets control of it.
That's where Defender comes in, since it runs with the highest privileges on the PC. SignDrop tricks the antivirus into opening a log the attacker prepared a…

articles.title: TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
articles.summary:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) confirmed that personal employee data has been leaked online after a threat actor put 6.9GB of information allegedly stolen from the company up for auction.
The technology giant said the incident affected current and former employees but doesn’t impact its operations or customers.
The company verified the leaked information and confirmed that it matched "data stored in the system services of a cloud service provider," indicating an external breach.
TSMC is the world’s largest contract chipmaker, manufacturing advanced processors and other semiconductors for companies such as Apple and Nvidia.
Last year, it shipped approximately 15 million 12-inch-equivalent wafers and generated $122.4 billion in annual revenue.
TSMC's investigation found that the leaked information matched data stored in a cloud service provider it uses, pointing to a breach outside its own infrastructure.
The company is now notifying impacted staff and providing the necessary support, while also engaging a third-party cybersecurity firm to help manage the situation.
“TSMC has found that some of our current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization,” TSMC says in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
“Currently, we have found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised,” the company added.

articles.title: 320 000 km et une batterie en pleine forme : cette étude de Ford réduit à néant la plus grande peur des automobilistes
articles.summary:
Acheter une voiture électrique est aujourd’hui gage d’économies substantielles vu les prix du carburant. Mais nombreux sont ceux hésitant encore à franchir le pas en raison du manque de recul sur le vieillissement des batteries. Quand l’on entend ici et là qu’il faut parfois débourser des dizaines de milliers d’euros pour changer un pack défectueux, il y a effectivement de quoi angoisser. Pourtant, il n’y a vraiment pas lieu de s’inquiéter…
Ford a en ce sens mené une grande étude sur les Mustang Mach-E vendus aux États-Unis et au Canada. L’analyse a porté sur 36 000 modèles datant de 2021, avec un peu plus de 5 ans au compteur, donc. articles.title: Can Indonesian researchers ever win a Nobel? Not without overhauling the research ecosystem
articles.summary:
Will Indonesia ever win the Nobel Prize? That question probably pops into some Indonesians’ minds whenever Nobel season starts in October.
The reality is that there are no shortcuts to a Nobel. Breakthroughs recognised by the committee almost always stem from foundational work done decades earlier — often when it is impossible to foresee the practical payoffs.
Take the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine awarded to Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel and Karl Deisseroth for pioneering optogenetics — a breakthrough technique that uses light to control nerve cell activity.
Read more: Bagaimana alga mengantarkan ilmuwan pada Nobel Kedokteran dan cara baru memahami otak
Interestingly, the road to optogenetics began with research that seemed to have nothing to do with medicine. Hegemann was initially investigating how the single-celled green alga Chlamydomonas swims towards light. His collaboration with Nagel eventually led to the discovery of channelrhodopsin — a light-sensitive protein that acts as an ion channel.
By 2005, Deisseroth’s team showed that channelrhodopsin could be harnessed to control neuronal firing with light. What began as a humble inquiry into pond algae laid the groundwork for optogenetics — now an indispensable tool for mapping and manipulating the brain.
This trajectory illustrates the road to the prestigious award: Nobel-worthy breakthroughs emerge from ecosystems patient enough to let basic research mature before demanding immediate benefits.

A quantum computer might seem to have little in common with a guitar, but researchers at ETH Zurich have found a surprising connection. Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. La plataforma no puede validar las prácticas de seguridad de estas aplicaciones. Por eso, los datos del usuario pueden quedar expuestos a riesgos que la versión oficial no presenta.

The FBI is warning that hackers are using an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks against organizations worldwide, including a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach that compromised Microsoft 365 customer environments.
In a FLASH advisory released Friday, the agency said multiple threat actors have weaponized the open-source framework since at least August 2026 to target organizations across the financial, government, technology, defense, healthcare, and other sectors.
"ARTEX significantly reduces the time required to chain attack techniques, with some intrusions progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours," reads the FBI advisory.
"The framework enables threat actors with minimal technical expertise to conduct complex, multi-target operations simultaneously, fundamentally accelerating attack velocity and expanding operational scale."
ARTEX is an autonomous penetration testing framework written in Go that uses artificial intelligence agents to perform reconnaissance, discover vulnerabilities, exploit systems, escalate privileges, and steal data with little human intervention.
Rather than using its own AI model, the framework integrates with external large language models (LLMs), including Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, Grok, and Kimi.

articles.title: Cómo crear presentaciones con Gemini Notebook para compartirlas en PDF o PowerPoint

Las presentaciones son, junto a los documentos PDF o las hojas de cálculo, un formato muy habitual para transmitir o compartir ideas o temas complicados de una manera más llevadera, práctica y ágil. Y aunque tiene sus detractores, son más los adeptos. Además, crear tus propias presentaciones es hoy muy fácil. Tanto como pedírselo a la IA. Sin ir más lejos, puedes crear presentaciones con Gemini Notebook, antes NotebookLM, con una simple frase.
Una de las facetas de Gemini Notebook, además de procesar fuentes y documentos, consiste en convertir los datos introducidos en otro formato de contenido. Por un lado, puedes ordenar tus notas, fotos, imágenes escaneadas y otros contenidos. Incluso puedes procesar libros en formato PDF o ePub. On Anthropic’s coding benchmarks, Fable 5.2 scored 49.1% at Xhigh effort on FrontierCode 2.0, compared with 45.5% for Opus 5.5 at Max. articles.title: España no está llena ni vacía: está concentrada, y este mapa lo demuestra
articles.summary:
El Instituto Nacional de Estadística dice que la población de España es de 49.801.559 personas a 1 de julio de 2026. La densidad poblacional de España es de unos 95-97 habitante/por kilómetro cuadrado frente a los 109,1 de la UE, es decir, que en España vive menos gente por kilómetro cuadrado que la media europea, pero es que además ya sabemos que sus habitantes no se distribuyen uniformemente: es lo que se conoce como la España vaciada. Pero es que en realidad la diferencia es tan abismal, que más que España vaciada, debería llamarse la España concentrada.
Este mapa muestra de un vistazo la enorme desigualdad de población que hay en España. Según datos del INE, el 40,9 % de la población vive en municipios de más de 100.000 habitantes y solo el 2,9 % en municipios de 1.000 habitantes o menos. Y si hablamos de crecimiento, Madrid y Catalunya por sí solas explican la mitad del crecimiento del estado desde 2015, como recoge elDiario.es.
El Ministerio de Política Territorial ya tiene diagnosticada esta despoblación desde hace tiempo y la enorme diferencia de densidad: hay un 48% de municipios por debajo de 12,5 hab/km2, y la mayoría de ellos tienen menos de 500 habitantes. Y todo apunta a que va a peor: la Estrategia para el Reto Demográfico describe que en España hay 78.000 localidades por debajo de los 100 habitantes, 23.000 más que en 1998.

Zu teuer: Warum Goldman Sachs den Zugang zu Claude Code und GitHub jetzt drastisch einschränkt
Die US-Bank Goldman Sachs hat für einige Mitarbeiter die Nutzung von KI-Tools eingeschränkt. Bislang durften die Goldman-Banker Anthropics Claude Code und GitHub von Microsoft nutzen. Laut einer ab Oktober geltenden Richtlinie beschränkt die Bank den Zugang zu den Tools nun auf Entwickler.
Die neue Vorgabe verärgert offenbar einige Trader der Bank, die die Tools bislang nutzen, um die Handelsströme von Kunden zu überwachen oder Marktveränderungen und Positionen zu modellieren. Das berichtet die Nachrichtenagentur Bloomberg aus vertraulichen Quellen.
Noch im Juli hatte CIO Marco Argenti das „Vibe Coding“ von Tradern und Bankern ausdrücklich gelobt. Mitarbeiter von Goldman nutzen bislang KI, um eigene Lösungen zu erstellen und übergaben dann die Ergebnisse an einen der 12.000 Entwickler der Bank zur Verfeinerung.
Nach dieser Experimentierphase sollen die KI-Tools nun aber wieder in die Hände derjenigen gegeben werden, „die am besten geeignet sind, sie langfristig zu nutzen“, wie ein Goldman-Sprecher sagte. Als Grund dafür nannte er das genauere Monitoring von Produktivität und Risikomanagement.
Die neue KI-Anweisung gilt nicht für sogenannte „Strats“, also Mitarbeiter, die an der Schnittstelle zwischen Handel, quantitativer Forschung und Softwareentwicklung arbeiten.

articles.title: The Sound of Smarter Farming - EE Times
articles.summary:
It was amid the stillness of the Covid-19 lockdowns that Conrad Young, founder and CEO of Chirrup.ai, realized that birdsong would make an excellent proxy for biodiversity. Birds have always acted as sentinels for changes in the environment, and as he told EE Times, “Birdsong is a pretty powerful and visceral way of understanding what’s going on in the environment but is also scientifically valid and benchmarkable.”
In March 2022, as the pandemic ended, Young launched Chirrup.ai to monitor birdsong and track farmland diversity. The first task was to deploy acoustic sensors and establish a baseline of bird activity that could provide a reference point against future recordings and reveal whether biodiversity was improving, declining, or remaining stable over time. Earlier trials used audiomoths—low-cost, acoustic loggers that record birdsong—but Chirrup.ai has now developed smart acoustic sensors.
The sensor pairs a MEMS analog microphone with a 24-bit digital audio codec, a 240-MHz processor with Bluetooth, and a high-speed 4G LTE modem. A multi-constellation GNSS receiver supporting GPS, GLONASS, and Galileo provides geolocation and timestamping for the acoustic data. The device is powered by a rechargeable lithium-polymer battery.

The Xbox arrived on Nov 15, 2001, during the sixth generation of consoles, facing stiff opposition from the legendary Sony PlayStation 2, Nintendo GameCube, and Sega Dreamcast. It would end up outselling Nintendo and Sega rivals, only living in the shadow of the PS2.

articles.title: Windows now runs on the iPhone Duo without a jailbreak
articles.summary:
In context: Apple's first foldable has only been in stores for about three weeks, and it's already running Microsoft's desktop operating system. A Google product lead has gotten the full Arm version of Windows 11 to boot locally on the iPhone Duo, without jailbreaking the phone. Fold it halfway, and the bottom screen becomes a keyboard and trackpad. Unfold it, and Windows takes over the whole 7.6-inch display.
The project, called WindowsiOS, comes from Ammaar Reshi, who leads product and design at Google AI Studio. He posted a demo on X this week and shared the full source code on GitHub, too. The demo shows a retail copy of Windows 11 24H2 running Microsoft Edge and Google's Antigravity coding app, all with touch controls.
Windows has technically run on an iPhone before. Back in 2024, the developer behind Tiny11 booted a stripped-down build on an iPhone 15 Pro using the UTM SE emulator. But it took roughly 20 minutes just to reach the desktop, mostly because UTM SE has to interpret every instruction in software.
 – Ammaar Reshi (@ammaar) November 11, 2026
The faster route of hardware virtualization is off the table, too, since Apple cut off hypervisor access on stock iOS starting with iOS 16.4. So instead, WindowsiOS translates Windows' Arm code into Arm code that the Duo's A20 Pro chip can run directly. Both sides already share the same instruction set – the same head start that recently let Switch games run natively on iPhones.

articles.title: DuckDB has an answer to “bloated” database messages
articles.summary:
DuckDB has an answer to “bloated” database messages
Older database protocols were built before big data. Some still send results row by row, repeating details like column names and types with every row. The result, says DuckLabs product team lead Guillermo Sánchez Dionis, is “quite a bloated message.” That overhead adds up when you’re moving large query results.
DuckDB’s answer is Quack, an HTTP-based protocol that streams query results in batches of column data as DuckDB produces them. It was previewed in May and was released in October as part of DuckDB 2.0.0 LTS.
On this latest episode of The New Stack podcast, recorded at DuckLabs headquarters in Amsterdam, Sánchez Dionis explains how that design lets developers start working with results while a query is still running.
A database protocol is a formal set of rules and message formats that dictates how a client application communicates with a database server. It acts as a specialized language that lets a software application securely send SQL queries, receive structured data tables, and manage transactions over a network. It handles connection and authentication, query packaging, data serialization, and error management.
But according to Sánchez Dionis, most protocols were designed pre-big data for other types of systems, with serialized rows rather than columns. They also add a lot of unnecessary data, he says, like column types and column names per row.

Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress.
Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
Following revelations about Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy Congress wants to crack down.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has already said that Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has also sent letters to both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling on them to publicly testify to the committee.
Bills such as the Remote Access Security Act, first introduced in the House in April 2025 but stalled in the Senate, are receiving renewed interest. While that specific bill might not become law, House Speaker Mike Johnson has said there is “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China,” according to Reuters. articles.summary:
Ya hace casi cuatro años del momento ChatGPT. Ese día en que todo empezó a cambiar. En estos casi cuatro años hemos tendido a medir la IA por lo bien que habla. Si escribe como una persona, si tiende a darnos la razón y dorarnos la píldora o si en cambio es asertiva y sabia, si es capaz de soltar un párrafo convincente en dos segundos... El espectáculo de la IA ha estado ahí, en la conversación.
La próxima gran apuesta de Google y OpenAI es una IA que no dice nada.
Se llaman modelos de decisión, y no escriben nada. Les das un contexto y una pregunta cerrada ("¿este correo es urgente?", "¿a qué departamento lo envío?", "¿qué herramienta debería usar ahora?") y te devuelven una opción junto a un número. Ese número expresa el nivel de confianza que tienen en su respuesta. Y nada más. En unos 150 milisegundos y por muy poco dinero.
Estos modelos de decisión fueron inventados por una startup llamada TypeSafe en septiembre. Su modelo, Jev, gustó tanto que la empresa ya valía 7.500 millones de dólares tres semanas después. OpenAI sacó el suyo unas semanas después. Y Microsoft y Amazon, en octubre. Google lo ha hecho esta semana.
Cuando todos los gigantes de la tecnología corren hacia el mismo sitio, algo pasa.
"Lo que pasa" es básicamente la factura. Hemos pasado del gasto alegre y derrochón en IA a un escrutinio cada vez mayor. Y cada vez más de ese gasto no lo generan personas directamente, sino sus agentes, los programas que trabajan solos y que en cada paso tienen que tomar pequ…

articles.title: Nearly 150,000 people sign petition requesting Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO
articles.summary:
What just happened? Three days after Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia's CEO, a campaign to bring him back is gathering momentum. More than 150,000 people have signed an open letter urging Nvidia's board to reinstate its co-founder while an independent investigation runs its course. Among those backing the effort are Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and thousands of people who identify themselves as Nvidia employees and shareholders.
The campaign, Stand with Jensen, comes at the end of an extraordinary week for the world's largest chipmaker. Nvidia has lost the only CEO it has ever known, its shares have taken a beating, and its board is searching for a successor just as fresh questions emerge about how Huang built and financed the AI boom.
The letter's organizers argue that Huang was forced out without being given a fair opportunity to defend himself. They are asking the board to do three things: reinstate him as CEO while the investigation continues, ensure he receives a fair hearing, and publicly explain the reasoning behind his departure.
The petition has attracted support from across Silicon Valley. In addition to Musk and Sweeney, signatories include Replit CEO Amjad Masad and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan.
By Sunday, thousands of signatories identified themselves as current Nvidia employees, with tens of thousands more claiming to be shareholders. The campaign notes that these are self-reported and have not been independently verified. It also says the effort is n…

articles.title: Cette app française connaît mieux votre Tesla que l'app Tesla
articles.summary:
Copeel est disponible sur l’App Store depuis le 12 novembre 2026, après « plus d’un an de développement », selon l’annonce publiée sur son site. Nous la testons depuis une vingtaine de jours sur un Model Y 2026 et nous ne pouvons que reconnaître la qualité et la pertinence des données de l’app. Copeel se connecte à votre compte Tesla et garde une trace de tout ce que fait la voiture : tracé et coût de chaque trajet, énergie consommée, recharges, autonomie et usure de la batterie au fil des mois.
L’éditeur et concepteur de l’app est Jordan Couturier, qui nous racontait il y a quelques mois sa vision : « L’objectif est que l’application ne soit pas seulement un tableau de bord de données, mais un véritable compagnon pour les propriétaires, qui les aide à mieux connaître leur véhicule, découvrir de nouveaux endroits et profiter davantage de leur expérience au quotidien. ».
L’idée n’est pas neuve : l’application officielle de Tesla reste assez avare en historique, et on avait déjà listé ce qu’il lui manque pour être parfaite (quelques mises à jour ont corrigé des défauts cités dans notre article, mais elle n’exploite toujours pas l’intégralité des données fournies par la voiture). Des outils comme TeslaMate (à héberger soi-même) ou Tessie comblent ce vide depuis des années. Copeel joue la carte de l’app native iPhone, en français, avec des données hébergées en Europe.

articles.title: Windows 11 öffnet heimlich eine Kopie deines Browsers, wenn du auf Links klickst: Das ist der Grund
articles.summary:
Kurz gestartet, heimlich wieder geschlossen: Was Windows 11 im Hintergrund treibt, wenn du auf einen Link klickst
In manchen Bereichen fühlt sich Windows 11 trotz seiner modernen Elemente recht langsam an. Das hat auch Microsoft erkannt und arbeitet seither daran, seinem Betriebssystem einen Geschwindigkeits-Boost zu verpassen. Einer dieser Bereiche mit Optimierungspotenzial ist für User:innen im Alltag nicht direkt ersichtlich. Es betrifft das Öffnen von Browsern und das Klicken von Links außerhalb der Programme.
Windows 11: Was passiert beim Klick auf einen Link?
Falls du Browser wie Chrome nutzt, um unter Windows 11 zu surfen, kann sich das Öffnen von Links gelegentlich recht langwierig anfühlen. Klickst du etwa in einer Mail auf einen Link, gibt das Betriebssystem diesen nicht einfach direkt an Chrome weiter – selbst, wenn das Programm schon läuft. Stattdessen öffnet Windows 11 eine weitere Instanz des Browsers. Durch den Prozess wird überprüft, ob die Anwendung schon aktiv ist. Ist das der Fall, wird sie heimlich wieder geschlossen und der Link schließlich an das gewünschte Ziel weitergegeben.
Das passiert immer dann, wenn ein Browser schon einmal seit einem Neustart von Windows 11 gestartet oder ein Link außerhalb des Browsers angeklickt wird. Wird ein Link geöffnet, wenn Chrome in der aktuellen Sitzung noch nicht geöffnet wurde, dauert es ohnehin etwas länger. Denn so muss Windows 11 erst das komplette Programm starten. articles.title: ¿De qué va ‘Ramayana: El nacimiento de una leyenda’, la estrambótica película india de la que todo el mundo habla?
articles.summary:
Ramayana: El nacimiento de una leyenda es quizás el más ambicioso intento del cine indio de llegar a una audiencia universal. Eso, sin perder su tono monumental, épico y colorido. Bajo la dirección de Nitesh Tiwari (Dangal), esta colosal obra cinematográfica representa la primera entrega de una ambiciosa bilogía. Una adaptación que traslada a la gran pantalla la célebre epopeya de la mitología india atribuida tradicionalmente al sabio Valmiki. Pero además, juega con la idea de que toda la mitología del mundo se conecta entre sí, entre la grandeza, la emoción y el sentido de la justicia.
Con un presupuesto histórico estimado de 4,000 millones de rupias (aproximadamente 500 millones de dólares), la película trasciende las fronteras de la industria de Bollywood. Todo, para proponer un espectáculo de escala operística, a menudo comparado por la prensa especializada de su país como la versión oriental de La Odisea. O una respuesta mitológica a grandes sagas contemporáneas, combinando cultura pop e historia en un escenario estrambótico.
Lo cierto es que Ramayana: El nacimiento de una leyenda es todo un evento fílmico a una escala muy poco común. Tanto como para trascender las fronteras de India y transformarse en un punto de interés de los últimos meses de 2026. Todo gracias a su firme propósito de universalizar un texto sagrado y cultural que ha influido por siglos en las tradiciones del sur de Asia. articles.title: Coreia do Sul investiga 1º colocado em prova após fraude com IA
articles.summary:
A polícia da Coreia do Sul abriu uma investigação após o candidato com a maior pontuação em um exame nacional para contadores fiscais confessar que utilizou inteligência artificial (IA) para responder às questões.
Ele ficou em primeiro lugar nas duas etapas da prova, realizadas em abril e julho. Na primeira fase, obteve 397,5 dos 400 pontos possíveis e errou apenas uma das 160 questões, desempenho que levantou suspeitas de fraude.
Candidato fotografou questões e consultou IA
Inicialmente, o candidato foi suspeito de utilizar óculos inteligentes para obter as respostas, mas negou a acusação. A confissão veio neste domingo (15), quando a Agência de Polícia Metropolitana de Seul anunciou ter recebido uma declaração por escrito, apresentada pelo advogado do candidato.
“Esta manhã, recebemos uma confissão por escrito, por meio do advogado do candidato, a respeito da fraude no concurso de contador fiscal”, declarou a instituição.
Em um vídeo publicado no canal de seu advogado no YouTube, o candidato explicou como realizou a fraude. Ele usou uma câmera em miniatura para fotografar as questões e enviou as imagens a uma ferramenta de inteligência artificial. Depois, consultou as respostas pelo smartphone.
“Usei uma câmera em miniatura para fotografar as questões do exame e as enviei para uma inteligência artificial; depois conferi as respostas no meu smartphone”, afirmou. Na mesma gravação, declarou que “lamenta profundamente” o ocorrido.

articles.title: Google turned to AMD Epyc, not its own Axion chips, to secure its first confidential TPU
articles.summary:
Google turned to AMD Epyc, not its own Axion chips, to secure its first confidential TPU
The reason says a lot about where trust in AI hardware really lives
- Google's new TPU 8tx pairs TPU 8t silicon with 5th Gen AMD Epyc "Turin" hosts to deliver confidential AI inference
- The AI juggernaut passed over its own Axion CPU, which hosts the 8t and 8i, likely because its audited confidential stack is x86-only for now
- The confidential TPU joins a growing number of chips even as key security details remain unpublished, even as Google and Nvidia already offer confidential GPUs to cloud customers
Google has added two more systems to its eighth-generation TPU family, and the one built for confidential AI leverages a host processor Google didn't design.
The TPU 8tx, detailed alongside the dual-chip TPU 8i Max in a Google Cloud blog post, pairs Google's accelerator silicon with 5th Gen AMD Epyc CPUs.
AMD also announced that Epyc forms the host foundation for what both companies call the first cloud TPU system with hardware-enforced confidential computing.
The same chip with a new trust boundary in tow?
Google's April 2026 launch split its eighth generation hardware into the TPU 8t for training and the TPU 8i for inference. Google bills this as the first time it has introduced four TPU systems in one year, but as ServeTheHome points out, the two newcomers are system configurations built on existing chips rather than new designs.

articles.title: Pourquoi les États-Unis ont cloué des avions au sol dans tout le pays pendant plus de quatre heures
articles.summary:
Les équipes de L3Harris, prestataire de l’aviation civile américaine, remplaçaient des câbles en cuivre par de la fibre optique sur un site isolé. Après leur intervention, le réseau des contrôleurs aériens a été saturé, et plus aucun avion n’a pu décoller des États-Unis pendant plus de quatre heures.
Vendredi, peu avant 16 heures à New York, la FAA, l’Administration fédérale de l’aviation, a interdit tout décollage dans le pays, avant de lever cette interdiction nationale à 20 h 15. L’agence n’avait pris cette décision que deux fois depuis le début du siècle, le jour des attentats du 11 septembre 2001, puis en janvier 2023, après la panne de l’un de ses systèmes informatiques. Selon Cirium, société spécialisée dans les données aériennes, les compagnies ont annulé plus de 8 200 vols vendredi soir, et au moins 3 000 autres hier. Sean Duffy, le secrétaire aux Transports, a présenté samedi les premiers résultats de l’enquête, mais il ignore encore si L3Harris a commis une erreur ou installé un routeur défectueux.
La FAA a coupé deux connexions qui saturaient son réseau
Dans un premier temps, un porte-parole de la FAA a seulement évoqué des problèmes de communication dans plusieurs centres de contrôle, chargés de guider les avions entre les aéroports du pays. Les ingénieurs de l’agence ont cherché l’origine de l’instabilité du réseau. AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
- Date:
- November 14, 2026
- Source:
- University of California - Berkeley
- Summary:
- Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.
- Share:
More than 300,000 people in the United States die from sudden cardiac arrest each year. This deadly emergency occurs when the heart's electrical system suddenly fails, causing the heart to stop pumping blood. It can strike older adults with known heart conditions as well as seemingly healthy young athletes. Although implanted defibrillators can prevent some of these deaths, doctors have long struggled to determine which patients need them most.
Now, researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a previously overlooked warning signal in routine heart scans that could make it easier to recognize people at risk before a fatal event occurs.
The discovery was made using artificial intelligence trained on more than 440,000 electrocardiograms, or EKGs, collected in Sweden. articles.title: Anatomy of a CPU
articles.summary:
The CPU is often called the brains of a computer, and just like the human brain, it consists of several parts that work together to process information. Some take information in, some store it, some process it, and others send the results back out. In today's explainer, we'll go over the key elements that make up a CPU and how they all work together to power your computer.
This article is part of our Anatomy series, which dissects the tech behind every major PC component. If you want to go even deeper, our CPU Design series covers how processors are designed and built in much more technical detail. This article goes over some of those fundamentals at a higher level and brings them up to date with how modern CPUs actually work.
Compared to other articles in our Anatomy series (see the full list of hardware components below), this one will inevitably be more abstract.
When you're looking inside something like a power supply, you can clearly see the capacitors, transformers, and other components. That's simply not possible with a modern CPU since everything is so tiny and because chipmakers like Intel, AMD, Apple and Qualcomm only share their designs at a high level. The actual circuitry is proprietary, so the topics covered in this article represent the general features that all CPUs have.

China acaba de dar un paso de gigante hacia la aviación comercial eléctrica: la compañía aeronáutica estatal COMAC ha culminado con éxito el primer vuelo con tripulación de su avión comercial eléctrico, el CE-25A, del que hace tres años conocíamos su maqueta. Otros como el X1 de Heart Aerospace lo han logrado antes, pero ya sabemos cómo se las gasta China: ya domina en el segmento de los coches eléctricos y la gran maquinaria y ahora pretende hacer lo mismo con los vuelos. No obstante, lo más difícil está por llegar.
El hito. Este primer vuelo tripulado del CE-25A tuvo lugar el 14 de noviembre en Binzhou (Shandong) y en la aeronave viajaron tres personas: dos pilotos y un ingeniero de ensayos, según CGTN. Aunque el vuelo era autónomo, los pilotos supervisaban su comportamiento y podían intervenir en la cabina. Según los informes, la aeronave ejecutó la prueba con normalidad y cumplió con lo previsto.
El pasado dos de febrero realizó el primer vuelo sin tripulación y, tras 19 validaciones autónomas, según Air Data News, su prueba de fuego fue ayer. El avión estuvo en el aire 16 minutos y 38 segundos y en este tiempo recorrió 60,4 kilómetros.
Por qué importa. El primer vuelo tripulado del CE-25A con éxito es un check más dentro de su programa: permite evaluar el rendimiento del avión con persona a bordo y le acerca a su verdadero punto crítico: la certificación, tanto a escala nacional como internacional. articles.title: Entró en vigor: Es obligatorio tener en casa un protocolo de riesgos laborales para el servicio doméstico
articles.summary:
Los empleadores de servicio doméstico tienen la obligación de llevar a cabo una evaluación de riesgos y poner en marcha las medidas preventivas que sean necesarias. Hasta el día 14 de noviembre de 2025 disponían de tiempo para ello. A partir de esa fecha deben haber sido llevadas a cabo.

En el Real Decreto 893/2024 se incluye el desarrollo de la protección de la seguridad y salud en el servicio del hogar familiar tras haberse suprimido su exclusión de la Ley de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales. En él también se incluye la protección frente a la violencia y acoso en este ámbito.

articles.title: The Hidden Costs of Patchwork Business Tools - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Most businesses don’t notice workflow problems all at once. They show up slowly.
A team spends extra time chasing approvals. Customer information lives in three different places. Reporting takes longer than expected. Employees keep switching between tools just to complete one task. None of these issues seem dramatic on their own, but together they create a system that feels heavier than it should.
That’s the real cost of a patchwork technology stack. It’s not just about licensing fees. It’s about the drag created when software doesn’t work together in a practical, business-friendly way.
Why tool sprawl becomes a business problem
At first, adding new software feels like progress.
One platform helps with communication. Another handles project management. A third improves security. A fourth supports analytics. Before long, the business has assembled a full stack of specialized tools.
The problem is that specialized doesn’t always mean connected. When systems are disconnected, people become the bridge between them. Employees copy information manually, repeat tasks, and lose time moving between platforms. That slows execution, increases mistakes, and makes scaling harder.
For growing companies, this becomes more than a productivity issue. It becomes an operational risk.

articles.title: Un avion que vous n’entendez pas peut révéler où vous avez tourné une vidéo
articles.summary:
Le 2 novembre, le vidéaste Colsto, spécialiste de la géolocalisation à partir d’indices publics, a publié une démonstration de 29 minutes intitulée I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location. À partir des images d’une simple caméra de surveillance (des arbres, une rivière et rien d’autre), il affirme avoir retrouvé l’endroit du tournage à une centaine de mètres près, en ne connaissant que le jour de l’enregistrement et le pays. Son seul indice : deux avions à hélice passés hors de portée de l’oreille, dont la trace subsiste dans les basses fréquences de la bande-son.
Comment un avion que vous n’entendez pas peut-il vous trahir ?
Tout part de l’effet Doppler, celui qui fait baisser la sirène d’une ambulance une fois qu’elle vous a dépassé. Un moteur d’avion produit le même glissement de fréquence, y compris à plusieurs kilomètres de distance. Les sons graves portent loin, et un micro de téléphone ou de caméra les capte là où votre oreille ne perçoit rien. Sur un spectrogramme, la représentation visuelle des fréquences d’un enregistrement, chaque survol dessine une courbe en S dont la forme livre la vitesse de l’appareil, sa distance minimale et l’instant exact de son passage.
L’autre moitié de l’équation vient des avions eux-mêmes : presque tous diffusent en continu leur position, leur altitude et leur vitesse via le protocole ADS-B, que des réseaux d’amateurs archivent jour après jour. Dans sa démonstration, le vidéaste repère deux survols espacés de 920 secondes, en…

articles.title: Arbeitstrend Microshifting: So soll er die Produktivität steigern und Stress reduzieren
articles.summary:
Statt 9-to-5: Warum immer mehr Beschäftigte im Homeoffice auf „Microshifting“ setzen
Die Arbeitswelt bringt immer wieder neue Trends hervor, die den Arbeitsalltag von Angestellten bestimmen. Selbst außerhalb des Büros, im Homeoffice, gibt es Trends wie den Soft Off Day, um dem immer anwachsenden Arbeitspensum und Druck zu entgehen. Der Trend Microshifting schlägt in eine ähnliche Kerbe, lässt aber die Produktivität nicht auf der Strecke.
Was ist Microshifting?
Bei Microshifting geht es darum, den Arbeitstag nicht als 9-to-5-Block zu sehen, sondern ihn in kleinere Blöcke aufzuteilen. Nicht jeder der Blöcke muss dabei zwangsläufig mit Arbeit gefüllt sein. Dank des flexiblen Homeoffice können Arbeitende etwa um 8 Uhr ihren Arbeitstag beginnen und die wichtigsten Aufgaben erledigen, bevor sie dann einen kurzen Block einschieben, um beim Supermarkt um die Ecke Erledigungen zu machen.
Danach wird wieder bis zur Mittagspause gearbeitet. Statt nur schnell etwas zu essen, verlängern Arbeitnehmer:innen dann die Pause etwas und bringen noch eine schnelle Session im Fitnessstudio unter, bevor es für einen weiteren Block wieder an den Arbeitsplatz geht. Zu guter Letzt holen sie noch den Nachwuchs aus der Kita und loggen sich ein letztes Mal von Zuhause ein, um den nächsten Arbeitstag vorzubereiten.
Obwohl im Laufe des Tages auch viele Aufgaben im Haushalt und des persönlichen Lebens erledigt wurden, kommt die Arbeit nicht zu kurz. Microshifter:innen behalten den Überblick über alle anlieg…

articles.title: Why companies still send contracts as email attachments - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
A quote is approved within the CRM system. The client agrees, the price is set, and yet, a peculiar ritual often begins: someone downloads a Word file, fills in the details, and emails a PDF.
The recipient prints it out, signs it, and sends back a scan. Or worse, they return a modified version, with no clear indication of what exactly has been changed. Meanwhile, the software remains completely unaware of these developments.
The problem isn’t the PDF itself
Sending a PDF is not, in itself, a bad practice. The format is widely supported and well-suited for sharing documents with a fixed layout. The issues arise primarily around the file. Who has the latest version? Is the recipient authorized to sign? And how does the finance or administration department know that the agreement has been finalized?
An e-signature platform can handle part of this workload. Through a feature like ‘request a signature,’ the client receives a request to sign the contract digitally, allowing the sender to track its status. However, simply replacing an email attachment with a link does not constitute a fully automated process.
A CRM system is not a document archive
Consider a supplier that enters into dozens of maintenance contracts every month. The terms are stored in the CRM, invoicing is handled via accounting software, and the documents end up in a shared folder. articles.title: Elizabeth Wakefield, asesora financiera: “Tener todo el dinero en una cuenta corriente es uno de los principales errores que mucha gente comete”
articles.summary:
Una buena forma de empezar a controlar tus finanzas es separar tus fondos en diferentes cuentas. Por ejemplo, no conviene poner todos tus ahorros en la cuenta en la que tengas los fondos con los que pago los recibos. Y es que esto es algo que viene bien hacerlo desde el principio. Elizabeth Wakefield es una asesora financiera que ha participado en el pódcast “Tiene sentido”, donde ha recomendado esta separación.
Por ello, es importante diferenciar el dinero que tenemos en nuestra cuenta corriente, ese que usamos para realizar nuestras operaciones diarias, de nuestro colchón de seguridad.
Por ejemplo, es muy parecido a cómo organizamos nuestra casa. Los calcetines no se pueden mezclar con los tenedores ni con ninguna herramienta. Cada cuenta debe cumplir un objetivo. De esta forma sabremos cuánto debemos destinar a cada necesidad antes de usarlo.
Separar los recibos, las emergencias y las vacaciones
La primera cuenta es la principal. Aquí son los ingresos los que entran y los pagos habituales los que salen. Es decir, aquí es donde gastamos nuestro dinero.
En este caso es recomendable abrir una nueva cuenta (preferentemente con intereses) que será nuestro colchón de seguridad. Es decir, es el dinero que vamos a usar en caso de urgencia. Por tanto, no es conveniente que sirva para pagar las compras habituales del mes.

articles.title: Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
articles.summary:
United Launch Alliance (ULA) suffered what is reportedly its first mission failure in its 20-year history, failing to deliver 40 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit. Leo is Amazon’s competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink, but it has struggled to get off the ground so far, putting only a small portion of the necessary satellites to challenge Starlink into orbit. Today’s launch was supposed to be the first of 38 flights Amazon purchased from ULA.
Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
ULA said an ‘anomaly’ led to its Vulcan vehicle failing to deliver its payload to orbit.
In a statement posted on X, ULA said, “Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit.”
The company said it was currently unclear what caused the failure, but pledged transparency as it continues its investigation. Amazon projected confidence in its launch partner despite the failure, posting on X that, “ There is risk with any launch, and that’s especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01. ULA has been a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they’ll learn from this mission and deliver on their long-term plans for Vulcan.”

articles.title: Today I learned why wind farms paint one turbine blade black
articles.summary:
Today I learned why wind farms paint one turbine blade black
And why newer offshore farms are now trying red
You'd think that painting a single turbine blade black is a pretty inexpensive fix for accidental bird deaths. It sounds almost too good to be true, which perhaps it is.
At the Smøla wind farm in Norway, every wind turbine had one of its blade painted black for an extended science experiment back in August 2013. Over the next three years, the number of bird carcasses found fell by 70%.
However, similar experiments in the Netherlands did not yield positive results, because apparently this fix depends heavily on the local bird species and population size.
Too many dead birds
There are a total of 68 turbines at the Smøla wind power plant, an archipelago off the coast of Central Norway. Researchers from the Norwegian Institute for Nature Research compared four regular turbines with four neighboring ones that had one blade painted black for this experiment.

Um exemplo estudado pela ciência é a professora de imunologia Aimee Pugh Bernard, da Universidade do Colorado, nos Estados Unidos. Ela costuma dormir perto das 22h e acordar por volta das 4h30 com energia para passear com o cachorro, treinar por uma hora na academia e trabalhar por uma hora e meia antes das 8h. Seu pai e seu irmão apresentam uma rotina semelhante.
Em 2019, Bernard descobriu ser portadora de uma mutação associada ao sono curto natural familiar (FNSS, na sigla em inglês). A condição hereditária faz com que algumas pessoas durmam naturalmente entre quatro e seis horas e meia por noite. Para confirmar a suspeita, ela enviou uma amostra de sangue à equipe de pesquisadores da Universidade da Califórnia em São Francisco.
Segundo a bióloga molecular Ying-Hui Fu, principal pesquisadora da equipe, os motivos pelos quais os portadores do FNSS parecem funcionar bem dormindo pouco ainda são investigados. No hizo carrera de periodismo. Entró en el mundo de la profesión gracias a su afición por los toros.

Esta situación también afectó a sus padres. Contó que no sabía cómo manejar ese dolor y que se lo pasó a sus padres. En “El Hormiguero” comentaba lo duro que era para una familia tener un hijo que está pasando por algo y que no encuentra la solución.

Toner dirige el Centro de Seguridad y Tecnologías Emergentes (CSET) de la Universidad de Georgetown. Según explicó, ambas compañías nacieron con la meta de construir máquinas tan inteligentes como las personas o más, y no con la idea de ser empresas de aplicaciones para consumidores.
El método se llama automejora recursiva: una IA que ayuda a crear la siguiente generación de IA. La idea es antigua. En la década de 1960, I. J. Good, que trabajó con Alan Turing, planteó que una máquina ultrainteligente podría construir otra todavía más inteligente.
Toner aclaró los límites actuales: las empresas no le piden a un modelo que se mejore solo, dijo, sino que usan IA en más partes de su proceso de investigación y desarrollo, y afirman que ven cómo ese trabajo se acelera. Mucha gente fuera de las compañías lo duda; muchos dentro lo creen.
Citó al ejecutivo Demis Hassabis, de Google DeepMind, quien habló de estar “en las estribaciones de la singularidad”, el momento hipotético en que la IA superaría a la humana. Para Toner, esa meta se volvió tan habitual en el mundo tecnológico de California que sus protagonistas pierden de vista lo extraña que suena para el resto.

Microbiologists modified an Ender 3 FDM printer to print macrostructures from microbes and make research on engineered living materials more accessible.
Microbiologists at the University of Rochester modified an Ender 3 FDM 3D printer into a 3D bioprinter for engineered living material (ELM) research. The team used SolidWorks to create the 3D model and sliced it in Slic3r, akin to a normal 3D printing workflow, with modified settings for the custom syringe pump print head. The $450 3D bioprinter makes ELM research more accessible, as bioprinters usually cost over $100,000.
Synthetic biology is like combining engineering with microbiology, treating microbes as machines and physical building blocks to achieve various functions. In the journal ACS Applied Polymer Materials, biologist Anne S. Meyer et al. published a 3D Bioprinting of Engineered Living Materials paper in August. The paper says that synthetic biology and 3D bioprinting have advanced ELM research, but the hardware costs and the inability of the expensive hardware to maintain the structure limit further progress. Hitting two birds with one stone, the researchers built an open-source, affordable 3D bioprinter from an Ender 3 and created their own support slurry, allowing the ELMs to keep their shape.

Je n’aimais pas le design du Honor Magic 8 Pro. C’est comme ça. Cela doit être dit, et je sais, tous les goûts sont dans la nature, mais je préfère bien plus la proposition du nouveau Honor Magic 9 Pro Max que j’ai pu prendre en main en amont de son lancement en France.
Mieux que l’iPhone sur certains points
Oui, il est vrai, il emprunte beaucoup à l’iPhone. Jusqu’à son nom. Mais il a aussi l’intelligence de s’inspirer du niveau de finition de la marque à la pomme avec un corps unibody, comprendre d’un seul tenant entre le cadre et le dos du smartphone, plutôt réussi. Cela offre un confort premium en première prise en main que seul l’unibody peut offrir.
Il existe toutefois une différence notable, qui ne sautera pas forcément aux yeux. Les incises dans les tranches pour les antennes sont bien plus fines que la plupart des concurrents de ce Honor, y compris l’iPhone 18 Pro Max. Pour continuer sur la finesse, il faut saluer également celle exceptionnelle au niveau des bordures noires autour de l’écran. Un vrai régal. Dommage que ce bel écran quasi bord à bord soit perturbé par une pilule, nécessaire pour offrir un déverrouillage infrarouge. Là encore, toute ressemblance avec une autre marque est purement fortuite, bien sûr.
Partenariat avec Arri
Passons au module photo. Celui-ci marque déjà l’arrivée du nouveau partenariat photo de Honor avec l’apparition d’un nouveau logo Arri, du nom d’une marque de caméra très utilisée dans le cinéma hollywoodien.

articles.title: Jensen Huang envisagerait un come-back chez Nvidia, malgré l'enquête en cours — Frandroid
articles.summary:
En janvier, au CES de Las Vegas, Jensen Huang résumait le secret de sa longévité à la tête de Nvidia en deux règles : ne pas se faire virer, et ne pas s’ennuyer. La première n’a pas tenu. Dimanche 15 novembre, le Financial Times a pourtant révélé que l’ancien patron envisageait un retour et en avait discuté avec des proches, selon plusieurs sources. Ni Nvidia ni ses représentants n’ont souhaité commenter, trois jours seulement après l’annonce officielle de sa démission.
L’un de ses alliés affirme monter une « war room », une cellule de crise réunissant des dirigeants de la Silicon Valley, pour faire pression sur le conseil et obtenir le soutien de la Maison-Blanche, avec l’aval de Jensen Huang. Une lettre ouverte intitulée « Bring Jensen Back » a été soutenue par Elon Musk et Tim Sweeney, le patron d’Epic Games. Elon Musk martèle que les relations clés de Nvidia avec ses fournisseurs reposent sur la crédibilité personnelle de son fondateur, et que l’entreprise risque de perdre des contrats essentiels sans lui.
    Pour aller plus loin
Nvidia officialise le départ de Jensen Huang et confie les clés à sa directrice financière
            
Le précédent Sam Altman en tête
L’idée n’a rien d’inédit dans la tech. En novembre 2023, Sam Altman avait été réintégré à la tête d’OpenAI cinq jours après son éviction, sous la pression des salariés et des investisseurs, et Steve Jobs était revenu chez Apple douze ans après en avoir été écarté. articles.title: Measure AI by results, not number of agents deployed: Oracle senior executive
articles.summary:
Measure AI by results, not number of agents deployed: Oracle senior executive
Business leaders should pick an outcome they can measure, such as reducing the time spent resolving accounting errors or lowering transport costs, said, Natalia Rachelson, Senior Vice President, Applications Development, Oracle.
Businesses adopting artificial intelligence (AI) should start with a measurable goal and judge success by the improvement it delivers rather than the number of AI agents deployed, as the technology moves from helping employees to doing work for them, a senior Oracle executive said.
"It’s important to remember that the number of agents deployed matters less than the improvement they deliver," Natalia Rachelson, Senior Vice President, Applications Development at Oracle, told PTI.
Business leaders should pick an outcome they can measure, such as reducing the time spent resolving accounting errors or lowering transport costs, she said.
"It’s important to establish a baseline first so you can assess whether AI is making a meaningful difference," she noted.
Companies then need to get the basics right: reliable data, clear ownership of processes, appropriate controls, and employees who understand how to work with AI agents. The biggest gains come from parts of a process where work gets delayed or needs repeated manual intervention, she said.
The biggest misconception business leaders have, she said, is that AI is about doing the same work faster.

articles.title: The Essential Eight Explained for Small and Medium Australian Businesses - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
If you run a small or medium business in Australia, there is a good chance someone has asked you about the “Essential Eight” lately. It might have been an insurer, a larger client sending over a supplier questionnaire, or your own IT person suggesting it is time to tighten things up.
The name sounds official because it is. The Essential Eight is a set of baseline cyber security strategies published by the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD), and it has become the common yardstick for how well an Australian organisation protects its computers, accounts and data. This guide explains what the eight strategies are, how the maturity levels work and how a smaller business can make real progress without hiring a security team.
Where the Framework Comes From
ASD, through its Australian Cyber Security Centre, publishes a longer list of strategies to reduce the risk of cyber security incidents. The Essential Eight are the ones it treats as the starting point. They were written with internet-connected Microsoft Windows networks in mind, which describes most Australian offices, from a three-person accounting practice to a hotel group.
For most private businesses the framework is voluntary. Australian Government agencies are expected to work towards it, but a café owner or an engineering firm usually adopts it by choice. In practice, plenty of businesses end up meeting it indirectly, because cyber insurance forms, government tenders and larger customers increasingly ask about it.

articles.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
articles.summary:
Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are. The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical information from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine. Participants will use a new iOS app to ask medical questions and then rate the responses based on criteria including accuracy, detail, and relevance.
Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
The study will be conducted through a new app where participants can ask health questions and rate the responses.
The app is now available for download, and enrollment starts today, with Apple looking for up to 200,000 people to contribute. Participants 21 and older must be based in the US, and although the app doesn’t use Apple Intelligence, it does require an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 26 or later.
Study participants can use the app to ask health-related questions and receive easily understandable responses with links to peer-reviewed clinical sources. The app relies on text-based prompts, and while dictation is an option using the iOS keyboard, the app isn’t integrated with Siri or Apple Intelligence.

articles.title: SA’s Yoco secures $100m credit facility to scale merchant cash advances - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
South African fintech company Yoco has secured a US$100 million credit facility from US investment firm Victory Park Capital to expand its merchant cash advance operation.
Yoco builds tools and services to help small businesses accept card payments in-store and online, access loans, and manage their day to day activities. The startup has advanced more than ZAR6.5 billion (US$395 million) to over 40,000 merchants since 2018, working with specialist credit providers.
The company, which secured US$83 million in Series C funding back in 2021, has now secured a US$100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital, which will allow it to scale its cash advance operations, and gain greater control over the pricing and risk of its merchant loans.
The aim is to use the transaction data generated by merchants using Yoco’s card machines and online payment tools to assess businesses that traditional lenders may struggle to evaluate, helping the company turn its payments relationship with more than 200,000 businesses into a larger cash advance operation.
“We have spent a decade building an operating system that runs a merchant’s whole business, payments, point of sale, and now the decisions in between. Financing was the one layer we didn’t fully control. This facility changes that,” said Yoco CEO Carsten Holtkemeyer.

GTA 5 Boots on Nintendo Switch 2 via Native Recomp
PLK, a developer known in the PS5 jailbreak scene for tools like Payload Manager and the Y2JB Autoloader, is now working on a native recompilation of GTA 5 for the Nintendo Switch 2. His first clip on X shows the game booting past the Rockstar logo and into the North Yankton prologue, with characters moving inside the bank alongside the minimap and mission text. About two hours later, PLK shared a second video saying the shader glitches were fixed and that build instructions should arrive soon. There are no performance figures or resolution details yet, and no word on how far into the story it gets.
The port runs on kaiHEN, a homebrew environment and minimal custom firmware for the Switch 2 that was released this week. Its GitHub page says Switch 1 homebrew built on libnx can be compiled for the Switch 2, though it also warns that homebrew gets full system access, NAND included, so a malicious app could brick the console. Paralympics Productions got it working on the original Switch in September, at around 30 FPS with overclocking, until Take-Two sent a cease-and-desist and the group shut down on October 3. articles.title: Madrid ya está saturado, así que el mercado de la vivienda se está disparando ahora en Torrejón, Parla y Alcorcón
articles.summary:
Es lo más lógico. Si quieres comprar un piso en el centro de Madrid pero no tienes dinero suficiente acabas buscando alternativas en las afueras o municipios limítrofes, áreas en las que (en teoría) el mercado debería estar menos tensionado y los precios ser más asumibles. Lo mismo si hablamos de Barcelona, Valencia, Málaga o cualquier otra capital de provincia. El problema, como acaba de constatar un estudio de Tinsa by Accumin, es que esa onda de demanda está dejándose sentir con fuerza en las periferias, elevando sus precios y restándoles atractivo como plan B (o C).
Hay un dato clave para entenderlo: el “esfuerzo teórico”.
¿Qué es el “esfuerzo teórico”? Una ratio, un indicador matemático que básicamente mide la presión que debe asumir una familia española si quiere comprarse una casa. Para calcularlo se simula el porcentaje de renta que un hogar medio tendría que destinar al pago de la primera cuota de una hipoteca que financia el 80% del valor de la vivienda.
¿A cuánto asciende ese indicador ahora mismo? Según el último informe de Tinsa by Accumin, al 36,9%. Es decir, la compra de una vivienda se traga casi cuatro de cada diez euros de la renta familiar. Es un dato interesante por dos razones. Primero, porque supera lo que los expertos consideran un “esfuerzo razonable” (35%). Segundo, porque empeora la media del trimestre anterior (35,7%). La lectura más interesante llega sin embargo al analizar en detalle de cada región.

articles.title: Cada hectárea de plátano deja 220 toneladas de tronco tirado en el campo… y las fábricas brasileñas ya lo convierten en fibra para ropa, papel y bandejas de fruta
articles.summary:
Además del racimo que se recolecta en la planta del plátano, hay otros restos que pueden aprovecharse: las hojas y el pseudotallo. En Brasil se lleva a cabo un proyecto llamado Banana Têxtil donde han desarrollado una técnica para hacer tejido a partir de la fibra del pseudotallo. También están siendo objeto de investigación sus posibilidades en otros campos como papel o embalajes de frutas.
En este caso hablamos de 220 toneladas. Este dato es una estimación del total de subproductos obtenidos por hectárea y año, recogida en un estudio publicado en BioResources. Se trata de un conjunto de restos (diferentes partes de la planta) que se encuentran en el campo tras la recolección. Podría parecer que se trata solo de tronco, pero no es cierto.
No todo lo que queda en la finca es simplemente dejado ahí. En el mismo estudio explican que en Brasil se deja en el suelo para evitar la erosión, además de controlar malezas e incorporar abono orgánico. Por ello, su extracción les da un destino diferente.
Del pseudotallo a un tejido
Si bien generalmente se suele llamar tronco, en realidad se trata de un pseudotallo. Está formado por la superposición de las bases de las hojas. Es posible extraer de él las fibras celulósicas. Mediante técnicas mecánicas es posible eliminar los componentes no fibrosos.

articles.title: Bald kannst du dein Bauchfett via Smartwatch messen
articles.summary:
Schluss mit groben Schätzungen: Samsung will inneres Bauchfett künftig per Smartwatch-Radar scannen
Laut Robert-Koch-Institut hat jede:r dritte Erwachsene in Deutschland einen deutlich erhöhten Bauchumfang. Das kann ein Indiz für zu viel inneres Bauchfett sein. Allerdings können auch Normalgewichtige von dem gefährlichen viszeralen Bauchfett betroffen sein, das tief in der Bauchhöhle liegend die inneren Organe umgibt.
Galaxy Watch soll viszerales Bauchfett messen
Je mehr davon vorhanden ist, desto größer ist das Risiko für Herzinfarkt oder Typ-2-Diabetes, heißt es von der Deutschen Adipositas-Gesellschaft. Mit einer neuen Funktion will Samsung Nutzer:innen künftig dabei unterstützen, speziell das gefährliche viszerale Bauchfett per Galaxy Watch präzise zu messen.
Wie Android Central schreibt, hat Samsung ein entsprechendes Patent angemeldet. Statt wie bisher per BIA-Sensor (bioelektrische Impedanzanalyse) soll dabei aber ein Ultrabreitband-Radar (UWB) zum Einsatz kommen. Bisher hat noch kein Galaxy-Watch-Modell ein solches Radar an Bord.

Original Mass Effect composer Jack Wall has recalled working on BioWare's role-playing game (RPG), describing the collaborative project as a "rewarding" experience that reminded him of how important it is to work with other composers.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, where the Mass Effect 1 and 2 composer also reacted to BioWare's closure, Wall shared what it was like creating a sci-fi RPG score with Sam Hulick, Richard Jacques, and David Kates.
"This was the game that helped me understand the value, importance, and just how much fun and rewarding collaborating with other composers can be," Wall said. articles.title: Un propietario es obligado a retirar la cubierta de madera que había instalado en la pérgola porque la comunidad solo le dio permiso para poner un toldo de tela
articles.summary:
El propietario deberá retirar la cubierta de madera que ha colocado sobre la pérgola de su patio. El dueño de la casa había solicitado el correspondiente permiso a la comunidad para instalar una estructura desmontable con toldos beige (como en los otros patios). Así fue aprobado el proyecto de la obra. Sin embargo, finalmente no se hizo así. Los hechos han acabado en los tribunales.
La Audiencia Provincial de Granada confirma la sentencia del Juzgado de Primera Instancia número 11. El dueño de la casa puede mantener la estructura de madera, pero deberá retirar la cubierta que ha instalado. Y podrá seguir teniendo cubierto el patio con los toldos (que eran los que estaban autorizados).
Sobre los pilares y vigas de madera maciza se han colocado tablones. Además, se ha instalado una lámina asfáltica para que pueda salir el agua de lluvia. Esto sustituye a los toldos que figuraban en el acuerdo de la junta (aprobado unánimemente por los asistentes).
La estructura podía quedarse; la cubierta debía retirarse
Mediante la prueba pericial se han determinado cuáles son los aspectos que están dentro de lo autorizado. La estructura está dentro de lo autorizado. Por otra parte, la cubierta es “no autorizada”. Tiene problemas urbanísticos (exceso de edificación y carencia de licencia).
En consecuencia, la resolución de primera instancia no ha mandado desmontar la pérgola. Tan solo se trata de retirar el techo que se ha añadido.

articles.title: Cette étoile brillait fort tous les 113 jours et on sait enfin pourquoi
articles.summary:
Quand le télescope Chandra l’a captée par hasard en 2001 et 2002, l’étoile AT 2016blu n’avait pas tellement attiré l’attention.
Jusqu’au 12 janvier 2012, quand elle a explosé en ce qui ressemblait à une supernova, repérée par le programme de recherche de supernovae de l’observatoire Lick, en Californie. À ce moment-là, de nombreux télescopes à travers la planète se sont tournés vers elle – mais il y avait un problème. Non seulement le signal ne ressemblait finalement pas tant que ça à celui d’une supernova, mais en plus, l’étoile était toujours là et avait cessé de briller intensément.
Depuis, les astronomes ont observé un cycle – avec une période de brillance particulièrement forte qui revient environ tous les 113 jours (soit à peu près trois fois par an) – avant qu’AT 2016blu ne retrouve son état habituel. Dans une étude publiée ce lundi 9 novembre dans la revue The Astrophysical Journal, une équipe d’astronomes issus en grande partie de l’Université de Virginie avance une explication : un compagnon caché.
27 explosions depuis 2012
La scène se déroule à 30 millions d’années-lumière de la Terre – dans la galaxie NGC 4559. L’étoile AT 2016blu pèse au moins 33 fois la masse du Soleil. Les astronomes la surveillent depuis une quinzaine d’années pour vérifier si son cycle de brillance se poursuit régulièrement.

articles.title: Google selects 10 startups for inaugural Africa Applied AI Lab cohort - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Google has selected 10 startups for the first cohort of its Google Africa Applied AI Lab, which gives founders early access to Google AI models, technical mentorship and links to venture capital.
Based at the Accra AI Community Centre (AICC) in Ghana, the Google Africa Applied AI Lab is managed by the Google AI Futures Fund alongside Google Research. It aims to support founders from across the continent interested in using the latest AI research to address real-world, uniquely African challenges – and, in turn, “build Africa’s first generation of AI-native unicorn startups”.
Google received thousands of entries from startups across more than 45 African countries, and has now selected 10 to take part in the inaugural cohort.
Three of the selected startups are from Nigeria – Intron, which builds speech recognition that understands African accents and code-switching; Termii, which provides customer verification and messaging for financial services; and Vendy, which lets businesses run storefronts and take payments inside WhatsApp.
Uganda’s Crane AI Labs builds offline AI tools for health workers and schools on affordable phones; Kenya’s Satlyt turns satellites into computing nodes that process data in orbit; and Senegal’s Tolbi combines satellite imagery with voice guidance to help smallholder farmers.

articles.title: LG xboom Blast, análisis: es grande y pesa, pero es un altavoz Bluetooth mucho más versátil de lo que dejan caer su diseño y colores

articles.title: France-Turquie : où voir le match de foot en direct et en streaming ?
articles.summary:
Zinédine Zidane a connu son premier couac en tant que sélectionneur de l’Équipe de France. Les Bleus ont été battus 3 à 1 par l’Italie à San Siro ce jeudi 12 novembre, perdant alors la tête du classement du groupe 1 de la Ligue A de la Ligue des nations.
Mais pas de panique. L’Équipe de France termine la phase de groupes par la réception de la Turquie, qui n’a plus rien à jouer et a subi cinq défaites en autant de matchs. Normalement, les Bleus devraient s’imposer et terminer au minimum deuxièmes. Le choc entre la Belgique et l’Italie, décisif et programmé à la même heure, sera bien évidemment à suivre en parallèle pour connaître le classement final.
Où suivre le match entre la France et la Turquie ?
Quand a lieu le match entre la France et la Turquie ?
France-Turquie a lieu ce dimanche 15 novembre 2026, au Stade Atlantique de Bordeaux (l’ancien Matmut Atlantique, qui a perdu ce nom en 2025). Le coup d’envoi sera donné à 20h45.
Il s’agit de la sixième et dernière journée du groupe 1 de la Ligue A de la Ligue des nations.
France-Turquie est diffusé gratuitement sur TF1

articles.title: Energiesparen: Aufklärung oder Nudging – was wirkt wirklich?

Aufklärung oder Nudging – was hilft beim Stromsparen wirklich?
Energiesparen ist eine Frage der Motivation. Doch wie genau motiviert man Menschen am besten? Eine deutsch-schwedische Studie hat zwei Ansätze empirisch miteinander verglichen: Erstens das sogenannte „Nudging“ – also das mentale „Hinschubsen“ in Richtung energiersparender Verhaltensweisen. Zweitens den „Kompetenz-Boost“ – also die Aufklärung darüber, auf welche Weise sich Energie sparen lässt.
Für einen 24 Wochen langen Versuch rekrutierte das Forschungsteam 140 Studierende in einem Stockholmer Wohnheim und teilte sie in drei Gruppen auf. Die Mitglieder der Nudging-Gruppe bekamen über ein personalisiertes Dashboards wöchentlich mitgeteilt, wieviel Strom sie im Vergleich zum Durchschnitt der Teilnehmenden verbraucht haben – und wieviel im Vergleich zu den sparsamsten 15 Prozent. Das ganze wurde durch fröhliche oder stirnrunzelnde Emojis garniert.
Ein Sechstel eingespart
Die „Booster“ bekamen Aufkleber mit QR-Codes ausgehändigt, die sie auf ihre elektrischen Geräte kleben sollten. Über diese Codes konnten sie regelmäßig neue Spartipps aufrufen – etwa Rezepte zum Kochen mit der Mikrowelle, Hinweise zum Abtauen des Kühlschranks oder zur Reinigung des Radiators. Daneben gab es noch eine unbeeinflusste Kontrollgruppe.
Das zentrale Ergebnis: Beide Versuchsgruppen konnten ihren Stromverbrauch gegenüber der Kontrollgruppe um ungefähr ein Sechstel senken. Der Unterschied zwischen Nudging und Aufklärung war minimal.
